problem_type: Repeated temporary WebGL probes lack shared lifetime and disposal
symptom: Each waiting surface and status badge creates new GPU probe contexts on initialization and mount, even when only four effects are admitted
direct_cause: useReducedProcessMotion calls readProcessMotionCapability per consumer twice; the reader creates a canvas context without explicit disposal
class_root: Stable document renderer capability and live accessibility preference share a per-consumer probe lifecycle
affected_population: Waiting surfaces and status badges across many nodes, mount cycles and preference changes
internal_only_reason: Application-owned probe lifecycle. Read both actual hook consumers, serialized performance caller, and installed img-fx shared renderer cleanup; no new external API or dependency introduced.
invariants: Hook consumers share one renderer probe per Document
Temporary contexts are explicitly released when the browser exposes WEBGL_lose_context, including failed reads
System reduced-motion preference remains live and listener cleanup remains paired
readProcessMotionCapability remains self-contained when serialized into page.evaluate

door_reduction.why_not: Reader type owner, hook read/policy calls, waiting surface and status badge are distinct required doors. Generated union of door-map processMotionCapability.ts and useReducedProcessMotion; both consumers converge on the hook cache.

generality_proof: The shared hook caches only renderer state per document, so every consumer and remount reuses it while live media preference is read separately. The reader always releases its own temporary context, including callers serialized outside React.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Share document renderer capability while observing dynamic preference
Self-contained capability read and temporary context release

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Uses shared hook before effect admission; no consumer-local probe remains
Uses same hook even though status dot does not need its own GPU context
Serialized direct reader retains self-containment and now releases its context

recurrence.reason: Every additional node, mount or accessibility change can repeat context allocation
same_class_scan: Read GenerationWaitingSurface, GenerationStatusBar and waitingFxScenario serialized reader

prevention.invariant: One renderer probe per document for all hook consumers, with explicit temporary context disposal
prevention.failure_mode: Missing or throwing WebGL reads produce null renderer and reduced motion; disposal absence/error cannot turn a valid read into an exception
prevention.strategy: Document-scoped weak cache at the existing shared hook, separate dynamic preference reads, and reader finally cleanup

legacy_paths.rationale: Replace repeated renderer probes and unowned temporary context lifetime; preserve the one reader and hook API

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Application creates and owns these temporary contexts; no third-party runtime upgrade controls their lifecycle

migration: No persisted data changes. Renderer cache resets on new Document.
residual_risks: GPU switching within the same document is not proactively re-probed; reload refreshes capability
If WEBGL_lose_context is unavailable, temporary canvas lifetime relies on browser collection

invariant_owner_layer.why: All production consumers share this hook; direct reader tests separately prove cleanup and serialization
